_note: DISPLAY SCENARIOS, not measurements of the viewer's hardware. Geometry and luminance capability are separate axes. Every donor and metric reads its display assumptions from this file.

PHONE.what: phone in landscape, the 1920 x 820 content full width (~14 cm) at 30 cm (M2.6 target; stimuli/display_targets.json PHONE_TARGET)

DESKTOP.what: 27-inch 2560 x 1440 monitor at 60 cm, content 1:1 (stimuli/display_targets.json DESKTOP_TARGET)

SDR200.what: brighter SDR monitor/phone in normal mode, 1000:1

BRIGHT500.what: bright OLED-like SDR phone, 100000:1 (black set by the panel, not the room)

HDR1000.encoding: SMPTE ST 2084 (PQ), Rec.2020 container, P3-D65 limiting gamut

BRIGHT500_PQ.encoding: SMPTE ST 2084 (PQ), Rec.2020 container, P3-D65 limiting gamut
BRIGHT500_PQ.what: 500 cd/m^2 HDR-capable display (Rec.2100 PQ). Added for ACES 2, which has a 500-nit PQ output but no 500-nit SDR (gamma 2.2) output

DARK.what: dark room: the target night-viewing condition (required)

DIM.what: dim living room; reflected luminance = E * k / pi = 0.16 cd/m^2 (Mantiuk et al. 2008 display model, eq. 17)

primary_matrix: PHONE x {SDR100, SDR200, BRIGHT500, HDR1000} x DARK; sensitivity: DESKTOP x SDR100 x DARK, PHONE x SDR100 x DIM
display_model_for_metrics: L_displayed = black + (peak - black) * EOTF(code) + E_ambient * reflectivity / pi (SDR); PQ decoded absolutely and clipped to [black, peak] (HDR); decoded by d0/display_model.py for EVERY donor, so no donor is judged by its own display model
